column5: The species of the Esteso 1964 top is UNKNOWN (the plan says only spruce); Sitka is the FPL species with a full orthotropic set, not a claim about the specimen. Axis convention: material axis 1 = L (grain), axis 2 = R (across the growth rings, in the plane of a quartersawn plate), thickness = T, so shear_modulus_12 = G_LR, shear_modulus_13 = G_LT and shear_modulus_23 = G_RT, poisson_ratio_12 = nu_LR (strain along R per strain along L under stress along L). Moduli are static or quasi-static handbook values at about 12 percent moisture content, used here at audio frequency; the validity band omega 0 to 2 pi 2000 rad/s and T 280 to 320 K is the band in which this use is DECLARED by the pack author, not a measured band (wood storage moduli typically rise a few percent per decade of frequency). Loss: the nine viscosities are Kelvin-Voigt values V = eta x stiffness / omega_ref with omega_ref = 2 pi 200 rad/s (1256.64 rad/s), built from the directional loss factors named in the observation as V = D^(1/2) Q D^(1/2) / omega_ref (Q the reduced plane-stress stiffness, D = diag(eta_L, eta_R, eta_LR); the L-R coupling uses the geometric mean of eta_L and eta_R; the 16 and 26 entries are zero by the orthotropic axes; the through-thickness shear viscosities are eta x G / omega_ref). A Kelvin-Voigt viscosity makes the loss factor proportional to frequency; wood's loss factor is nearly constant, so a consumer must rescale per mode by omega_ref/omega (guitar_body_modes does). The loss factors are measured on other specimens and are NOT a measurement of the Esteso guitar.
